Service: Emergency department visit, level 5 (CPT 99285), CT angiogram chest  
Date of Service: October 11, 2026  

This is a formal request for a first-level internal appeal of the adverse benefit determination dated October 23, 2026, which denied coverage for the emergency department visit and CT angiogram chest performed on October 11, 2026, at St. Agnes Regional Medical Center. The denial stated: “Services were provided by a facility that does not participate in the Blue Meridian network. Your plan does not cover non-emergency services from out-of-network providers.” This reason is incorrect and contrary to the terms of the plan and applicable federal law.

The patient’s presentation with sudden sharp chest pain radiating to the back, shortness of breath, hypertension (BP 178/104), tachycardia (HR 118), and ESI level 2 triage constitutes an emergency medical condition under the plan’s definition and federal standards. As documented in the St. Agnes Regional Medical Center Emergency Department Record dated October 11, 2026, the chief complaint was “Sudden sharp chest pain radiating to back, shortness of breath, began 01:30 while driving on I-75,” and the patient arrived via EMS. According to Article 3 of the Blue Meridian plan, titled “EMERGENCY SERVICES,” an emergency medical condition is defined as “a condition manifesting itself by acute symptoms of sufficient severity, including severe pain, such that a prudent layperson, who possesses an average knowledge of health and medicine, could reasonably expect the absence of immediate medical attention to result in serious jeopardy to health.” The patient’s symptoms clearly meet this prudent layperson standard, necessitating immediate evaluation.

As an emergency service rendered at the nearest capable facility, the ED visit and CT angiogram are covered under Article 3 regardless of network status, and the denial’s reliance on non-emergency exclusions is inapplicable. Article 3 explicitly states: “Emergency services are covered in-network and out-of-network without prior authorization. Emergency services provided by an out-of-network facility will be covered at the in-network cost-sharing level.” Furthermore, the medical record confirms: “Note: Patient brought by EMS; St. Agnes was the nearest emergency department (4.1 miles).” Article 3, titled “OUT-OF-NETWORK SERVICES,” specifies that “Non-emergency services from out-of-network providers are not covered unless a referral has been approved by the Plan.” However, this restriction does not apply to emergency services, which are separately and expressly covered under Article 3.

Federal protections under the No Surprises Act and Article 9 of the plan prohibit balance billing and affirm coverage for emergency services at out-of-network facilities, rendering the denial contrary to binding law. Article 9, titled “BALANCE BILLING PROTECTIONS,” states: “For emergency services, members are protected from balance billing as required by federal law, including the No Surprises Act.” Additionally, Article 8, titled “CLAIMS AND APPEALS,” provides that “You may appeal an adverse benefit determination within 180 days. The Plan will provide a full and fair review in accordance with ERISA Section 503 and 29 CFR 2560.503-1.” As an employer-sponsored plan, this claim is governed by ERISA, and the plan administrator must conduct a full and fair review of this appeal.

Based on the plan’s emergency services provisions, the medical documentation of an emergency medical condition, and federal protections under the No Surprises Act, I request that you immediately overturn the denial, process the claim for payment at the in-network cost-sharing level, and waive any patient liability for balance billing. In accordance with your appeals process, I also request a peer-to-peer review between the treating physician and a medical director affiliated with Blue Meridian Insurance Co., and a complete copy of the claim file, including all criteria, clinical guidelines, and plan provisions used to make the initial determination.

Please acknowledge receipt of this appeal and provide a decision within the required timeframe for post-service appeals under your plan and ERISA guidelines.

Sincerely,  
[Signature]  
Marcus Oyelaran
